issues.legal_issue: A High Court should not entertain a writ petition challenging a Debt Recovery Tribunal order when an effective statutory appeal is available before the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal, particularly where the writ petition would circumvent the statutory pre-deposit requirement.
Publication and service of possession notices in accordance with the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 satisfy the notice requirements under Rules 8(1) and 8(2).
The 25% deposit requirement under Rule 9(3) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 is met when the purchaser deposits that amount on the day of auction or by the next working day.

Under Rule 9(4) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002, the secured creditor may extend the time for payment of the balance sale price, within the statutory maximum, and payment within the extended period complies with the rule.

A property is excluded from enforcement under Section 31(i) of the SARFAESI Act only if it was actually used as agricultural land when the security interest was created; its classification as agricultural land in revenue records alone is insufficient.
A borrower claiming that secured property is exempt agricultural land under Section 31(i) of the SARFAESI Act bears the burden of proving its actual agricultural use.
